messages.content:
Dear participants,

We have prepared a more challenging experimental dataset of 100 Order-5 Hard problems involving Austin laws. For each problem, at least one of Eq1 or Eq2 is an Austin law. The ground truth for some of these problems is currently unknown.

Experimental dataset:
https://huggingface.co/datasets/SAIRfoundation/equational-theories-selected-problems/viewer/research_order5_hard

For more background on Order-5 Austin laws, see the Equational Theories blueprint:
https://teorth.github.io/equational_theories/blueprint/order-5-austin-laws.html

These problems are intended only for experimentation and research. They will not be included in the main leaderboard evaluation.

Thank you for your participation and support!

messages.content:
@YZ

I took up the challenge for research_order5_hard_0014:

Eq1 = 40909 → Eq2 = 28770.

After working through Eq. 40909, I now have a Lean kernel-checked countermodel, so the implication is:

Equation 40909⇏Equation 28770\boxed{\mathrm{Equation}\ 40909 \not\Rightarrow \mathrm{Equation}\ 28770}Equation 40909⇒Equation 28770​

In other words, problem 0014 is FALSE.

There are a few structural facts about Eq. 40909 that may be worth recording, because the result turned out to be stronger than just deciding this implication.

Eq. 40909 is

((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y=x.((((y \diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z)\diamond y=x.((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y=x.

For fixed yyy, Eq. 40909 implies left cancellation:

y⋄a=y⋄b⟹a=b.y\diamond a=y\diamond b \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a=b.y⋄a=y⋄b⟹a=b.

Every right translation is also surjective.

More importantly, define

Φy(x,z)=(((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z.\Phi_y(x,z)=(((y\diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z.Φy​(x,z)=(((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z.

Then Eq. 40909 gives

Φy(x,z)⋄y=x,\Phi_y(x,z)\diamond y=x,Φy​(x,z)⋄y=x,

and one obtains an injection

Φy:G×G↪G.\Phi_y:G\times G\hookrightarrow G.Φy​:G×G↪G.

Therefore every finite nonempty model of Eq. 40909 is trivial.

Another useful consequence is that an idempotent collapses the entire model:

y⋄y=y⟹∀a,b, a=b.y\diamond y=y \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \forall a,b,\ a=b.y⋄y=y⟹∀a,b, a=b.

This gives a particularly short connection with Eq. 28770.

Under Eq. 40909, the diagonal instance of Eq. 28770 obtained by taking x=yx=yx=y and z=yz=yz=y forces

y⋄y=y.y\diamond y=y.y⋄y=y.

Hence, among models of Eq. 40909,

Eq28770⟺the model is trivial.\mathrm{Eq28770} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \text{the model is trivial}.Eq28770⟺the model is trivial.

So the original implication reduces to the real question:

Does Eq. 40909 admit a nontrivial model?

The answer is yes.

The construction came from an infinite recursive rewrite forest.

Orient Eq. 40909 as the initial rule

R0:((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y  ⟶  x.R_0:\qquad ((((y\diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z)\diamond y \;\longrightarrow\;x.R0​:((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y⟶x.

Suppose a branch has the form

A⋄p⟶q.A\diamond p\longrightarrow q.A⋄p⟶q.

Eq. 40909 generates the next branch

((((q⋄A)⋄A)⋄z)⋄A)  ⟶  p.((((q\diamond A)\diamond A)\diamond z)\diamond A) \;\longrightarrow\;p.((((q⋄A)⋄A)⋄z)⋄A)⟶p.

Iterating this produces an infinite family

R0,R1,R2,…R_0,R_1,R_2,\ldotsR0​,R1​,R2​,…

with a very rigid recursive structure.

During completion, the branch interactions exhibited the pattern

Ri⋈Rj  ⇝  Ri+j+1.R_i\bowtie R_j \;\leadsto\; R_{i+j+1}.Ri​⋈Rj​⇝Ri+j+1​.

This led to a forest formulation with a trunk, recursive branches, promotion, provenance, rank, and normal leaves.

The final proof does not depend on checking only finitely many critical pairs.

Instead, I construct the magma of hereditarily normal terms.

For two normal terms a,ba,ba,b, their product is defined by:

  • reducing a⋄ba\diamond ba⋄b if it is a root instance of one of the recursive rules RnR_nRn​;
  • otherwise retaining the raw node a⋄ba\diamond ba⋄b.

The main structural facts are then proved:

  1. root reduction is functional;
  2. every recursive rule strictly decreases term size;
  3. variables are irreducible normal leaves;
  4. the normal-term magma satisfies Eq. 40909;
  5. two distinct variables remain distinct.

A canonical normalization map nf\mathrm{nf}nf is then defined.

Every rewrite step preserves this normal form, and every term rewrites to its canonical normal form. Hence every local fork joins.

This gives the full local-join theorem

LocalForestJoin,\mathrm{LocalForestJoin},LocalForestJoin,

and global confluence follows from strict descent together with a measure-based Newman argument.

The final Lean certificate proves

∃G,G⊨Eq40909∧G⊭Eq28770.\exists G,\qquad G\models \mathrm{Eq40909} \quad\land\quad G\not\models \mathrm{Eq28770}.∃G,G⊨Eq40909∧G⊨Eq28770.

So the final result is

Eq40909⇏Eq28770.\boxed{\mathrm{Eq40909}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{Eq28770}.}Eq40909⇒Eq28770.​

There is also a stronger consequence.

Since every finite nonempty model of Eq. 40909 is trivial, while the constructed model is nontrivial, this model must be infinite.

Therefore Eq. 40909 itself admits a nontrivial infinite model.

So Eq. 40909 is an Austin law as well.

Eq. 28770 was already a known Austin law; thus problem 0014 gives an interesting situation where both sides are Austin laws, but the implication still fails.

The complete final Lean kernel check finished with:

EXIT_CODE=0

on my machine.

The final verification run took approximately 8m27s. The research and discovery process was, of course, substantially longer.

I would be very interested if someone wants to independently inspect the recursive RnR_nRn​ construction, the normal-term magma, or the forest-completion argument.

Now that 0014 is settled:

which one would you like me to look at next? :smile:

I genuinely love this research dataset.

@**YZ** 
I took a closer look at **research_order5_hard_0014**, i.e.

`Eq1 = 40909`, `Eq2 = 28770`.

Eq. 40909 is

$$
((((y \diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z)\diamond y=x.
$$

I now have a Lean-checked proof that

$$
\boxed{40909 \not\Rightarrow 28770}.
$$

A few intermediate facts about Eq. 40909 may be of independent interest.

For fixed $y$, the map

$$
x \mapsto (y\diamond x)\diamond y
$$

is injective.

Also, if

$$
\Phi_y(x,z)=(((y\diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z,
$$

then Eq. 40909 gives

$$
\Phi_y(x,z)\diamond y=x.
$$

Hence, for each fixed $y$,

$$
\Phi_y:G\times G\hookrightarrow G
$$

is injective.

Therefore every finite nonempty model of Eq. 40909 is trivial.

There are several other consequences:

$$
y\diamond a=y\diamond b \implies a=b,
$$

every right translation is surjective, and any idempotent

$$
y\diamond y=y
$$

forces the whole magma to be a singleton.

This gives a short bridge to Eq. 28770.

Under Eq. 40909, the diagonal instance of Eq. 28770 with $x=y$ and $z=y$ forces

$$
y\diamond y=y,
$$

and therefore forces the model to be trivial.

So, inside the class of Eq. 40909 models,

$$
\boxed{\mathrm{Eq28770}\iff \text{the model is trivial}.}
$$

Thus the problem reduces to one question:

> Does Eq. 40909 admit a nontrivial model?

The construction I found uses an infinite recursive rewrite forest.

Orient Eq. 40909 as

$$
R_0:
((((y\diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z)\diamond y
\to x.
$$

If a rule has the form

$$
A\diamond p\to q,
$$

then Eq. 40909 generates the next branch

$$
\boxed{
((((q\diamond A)\diamond A)\diamond z)\diamond A)
\to p.
}
$$

Iterating this gives an infinite family

$$
R_0,R_1,R_2,\ldots
$$

with a very rigid recursive structure.

The branch interaction that emerged is

$$
R_i\bowtie R_j \leadsto R_{i+j+1}.
$$

This suggested a forest description in terms of trunk, branches, promotion, provenance and normal leaves.

The final proof does not rely on a finite critical-pair search.

Instead, one constructs a magma of **hereditarily normal terms**.

For normal terms $a,b$, define their product as follows:

- if $a\diamond b$ is a root instance of some $R_n$, reduce it;
- otherwise keep the raw term $a\diamond b$.

The key points are:

1. root reduction is functional;
2. every recursive rule strictly decreases term size;
3. variables are irreducible leaves;
4. the resulting normal-term magma satisfies Eq. 40909;
5. two distinct variables remain distinct, so the magma is nontrivial.

A canonical normalization map can then be defined, and every rewrite step preserves its normal form. This gives the full local join property for the recursive forest and hence global confluence by a measure-based Newman argument.

The final Lean theorem is essentially

$$
\exists G,\quad
G\models \mathrm{Eq40909}
\quad\text{and}\quad
G\not\models \mathrm{Eq28770}.
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{\mathrm{Eq40909}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{Eq28770}.}
$$

Since every finite Eq. 40909 model is trivial, the nontrivial model constructed above is necessarily infinite.

So Eq. 40909 itself admits a nontrivial infinite model.

The final full Lean kernel check completed successfully with

`EXIT_CODE=0`

and took about **8m27s** on my machine.

The research/search phase was of course substantially longer than that final verification run.

I am happy to share more details if anyone wants to independently check the recursive $R_n$ family, the normal-term magma, or the local-confluence argument.

**Which one should I look at next? 😄**

I genuinely enjoy this dataset.

((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y=x.((((y \diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z)\diamond y=x.

I now have a Lean-checked proof that

40909⇏28770.\boxed{40909 \not\Rightarrow 28770}.

A few intermediate facts about Eq. 40909 may be of independent interest.

For fixed $y$, the map

x↦(y⋄x)⋄yx \mapsto (y\diamond x)\diamond y

is injective.

Also, if

Φy(x,z)=(((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z,\Phi_y(x,z)=(((y\diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z,

then Eq. 40909 gives

Φy(x,z)⋄y=x.\Phi_y(x,z)\diamond y=x.

Hence, for each fixed $y$,

Φy:G×G↪G\Phi_y:G\times G\hookrightarrow G

is injective.

Therefore every finite nonempty model of Eq. 40909 is trivial.

There are several other consequences:

y⋄a=y⋄b  ⟹  a=b,y\diamond a=y\diamond b \implies a=b,

every right translation is surjective, and any idempotent

y⋄y=yy\diamond y=y

forces the whole magma to be a singleton.

This gives a short bridge to Eq. 28770.

Under Eq. 40909, the diagonal instance of Eq. 28770 with $x=y$ and $z=y$ forces

y⋄y=y,y\diamond y=y,

and therefore forces the model to be trivial.

So, inside the class of Eq. 40909 models,

Eq28770  ⟺  the model is trivial.\boxed{\mathrm{Eq28770}\iff \text{the model is trivial}.}

Thus the problem reduces to one question:

Does Eq. 40909 admit a nontrivial model?

The construction I found uses an infinite recursive rewrite forest.

Orient Eq. 40909 as

R0:((((y⋄x)⋄y)⋄y)⋄z)⋄y→x.R_0: ((((y\diamond x)\diamond y)\diamond y)\diamond z)\diamond y \to x.

If a rule has the form

A⋄p→q,A\diamond p\to q,

then Eq. 40909 generates the next branch

((((q⋄A)⋄A)⋄z)⋄A)→p.\boxed{ ((((q\diamond A)\diamond A)\diamond z)\diamond A) \to p. }

Iterating this gives an infinite family

R0,R1,R2,…R_0,R_1,R_2,\ldots

with a very rigid recursive structure.

The branch interaction that emerged is

Ri⋈Rj⇝Ri+j+1.R_i\bowtie R_j \leadsto R_{i+j+1}.

This suggested a forest description in terms of trunk, branches, promotion, provenance and normal leaves.

The final proof does not rely on a finite critical-pair search.

Instead, one constructs a magma of hereditarily normal terms.

For normal terms $a,b$, define their product as follows:

  • if $a\diamond b$ is a root instance of some $R_n$, reduce it;
  • otherwise keep the raw term $a\diamond b$.

  1. root reduction is functional;
  2. every recursive rule strictly decreases term size;
  3. variables are irreducible leaves;
  4. the resulting normal-term magma satisfies Eq. 40909;
  5. two distinct variables remain distinct, so the magma is nontrivial.

A canonical normalization map can then be defined, and every rewrite step preserves its normal form. This gives the full local join property for the recursive forest and hence global confluence by a measure-based Newman argument.

The final Lean theorem is essentially

∃G,G⊨Eq40909andG⊭Eq28770.\exists G,\quad G\models \mathrm{Eq40909} \quad\text{and}\quad G\not\models \mathrm{Eq28770}.

Therefore

Eq40909⇏Eq28770.\boxed{\mathrm{Eq40909}\not\Rightarrow\mathrm{Eq28770}.}

Since every finite Eq. 40909 model is trivial, the nontrivial model constructed above is necessarily infinite.

So Eq. 40909 itself admits a nontrivial infinite model.

EXIT_CODE=0

and took about 8m27s on my machine.

The research/search phase was of course substantially longer than that final verification run.

I am happy to share more details if anyone wants to independently check the recursive $R_n$ family, the normal-term magma, or the local-confluence argument.

messages.content:
Hi everyone — a quick update on our order-5 experiments!

The solver we submitted to the competition about two weeks ago could already construct infinite models for 28 equations in ETP’s 96 order-5 Austin candidates. We kept working on the four proof-producing searches after the submission, and the number has now increased to 32. All 32 certificates have been accepted by Judge v3.

Here are the 32 equations, grouped into dual pairs:

  • E4952 / E41252
  • E4957 / E40914
  • E5012 / E41253
  • E5066 / E41239
  • E5141 / E40917
  • E5295 / E40909
  • E7701 / E38303
  • E7755 / E38249
  • E9345 / E36713
  • E9384 / E36714
  • E9667 / E36638
  • E9680 / E36524
  • E11081 / E35036
  • E11116 / E34888
  • E19966 / E26105
  • E22619 / E22634

Since these equations are already known to have only trivial finite models, the certificates confirm that all 32 are Austin laws.

We also found explicit infinite models for another dual pair:

  • E17260 / E28740

Their finite-model status is still open, so we are not calling them Austin laws yet. These two certificates have also been accepted by Judge v3.

A small note on prior work: four of the 32 equations—E19966, E26105, E22619, and E22634—also appear in the earlier ALPS results, although those classifications have not yet been reflected in the current ETP table.

We are writing up the method now and plan to release a paper, the Lean certificates, and a reproducible artifact soon. More details coming shortly!
